binders: There exists a real constant c, chosen uniformly before all other data.
For every finite type ι and every measurable space Ω.
For every probability measure μ on Ω.
For every real-valued family X : ι → Ω → ℝ, given that the universal finite index set is nonempty.
In each branch, for every real threshold t.
hypotheses: Every X_i is μ-integrable and centered: ∫ X_i dμ = 0.
Every individual exponential-moment gauge is strictly below infinity.
The family X is mutually independent under μ.
The first conclusion is conditional on K > 0, and the second is conditional on K = 0.
conclusions: Let n = card(ι), let K = max_i (gauge_μ(X_i)).toReal, and let M(ω) = Σ_i n⁻¹ X_i(ω). If K > 0, then for every t ≥ 0, μ({ω | |M(ω)| ≥ t}).toReal ≤ 2 exp(-c n min(t²/K², t/K)).
With the same n, K, and empirical average M, if K = 0, then for every t ≥ 0, μ({ω | |M(ω)| ≥ t}).toReal ≤ 2 when t = 0 and ≤ 0 when t ≠ 0.
mathematical_definitions: For a real function X, gauge_μ(X) is the ENNReal infimum of all s such that X is measurable, s is nonzero and finite, exp(|X|/s.toReal) is μ-integrable, and ∫ exp(|X|/s.toReal) dμ ≤ 2.
n is the cardinality of the nonempty finite index type, so n is positive.
K is the maximum of the real conversions of the individual finite gauges.
The random quantity in the event is Σ_i (card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ X_i, equivalently the empirical average n⁻¹ Σ_i X_i.
The positive-gauge exponent is -(c · min(t²/K², t/K)) · n, equivalently -c n min(t²/K², t/K).
Tail probabilities are represented by the real conversion μ.real of the corresponding event measure.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal positive constant c such that, for every nonempty finite mutually independent family of measurable, integrable, mean-zero real random variables with finite exponential-moment gauges, the empirical average satisfies a two-regime exponential tail bound. If K is the largest gauge and n is the family size, then at every nonnegative threshold t the tail is at most twice exp(-c n times the smaller of t squared over K squared and t over K), provided K is positive. If K is zero, the statement instead gives bound 2 at threshold zero and probability zero at every positive threshold.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type must be finite and nonempty; an empty average is not covered.
Nonemptiness implies n = card(ι) > 0, so the real inverse in the empirical average is the ordinary reciprocal 1/n rather than Lean's special inverse of zero.
The variables are real-valued on one probability space and must be measurable, integrable, exactly centered, and mutually independent.
Every individual gauge must be strictly below ENNReal infinity before conversion to Real and maximization.
The gauge is an infimum over nonzero finite admissible scales, and its definition alone does not assert that the infimum is positive or attained.
The main exponential formula is guarded by K > 0, so both K and K² denominators are nonzero there.
The K = 0 branch is substantive: at every t > 0 its right side is zero, forcing the empirical average to exceed no positive threshold with positive probability.
Only thresholds t ≥ 0 are covered. At t = 0 the zero-gauge branch uses the coarse bound 2.
The proposition conjoins implications for K > 0 and K = 0. Their exhaustiveness uses the mathematical nonnegativity of K, inherited from maxima of converted ENNReal gauges.
μ.real is safe as an ordinary real probability under the probability-measure assumption; without finiteness, ENNReal.toReal would map infinity non-faithfully.
ambiguities: The local infimum-defined gauge has the form of a psi-one/Orlicz exponential-moment gauge, but the packet supplies no conventional name; its explicit definition is controlling.

The packet does not establish within the definition itself why gauge zero forces the zero positive-threshold tail asserted in the second branch, though that assertion is unambiguously part of the proposition.
No source context is available to determine whether the explicit K = 0 branch is an endpoint completion of another displayed formula or was independently intended.
